title: AES-256 logical-circuit Grover key search (GLRS2016)

target.description: Full 14-round AES-256 key search from 5 suitable classical known plaintext/ciphertext pairs. Table 5 estimates the complete Grover search, not one reversible AES evaluation or a physical machine.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: All master keys in the stated attack model; no weak-key restriction is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 5 suitable distinct known plaintext/ciphertext pairs under the same key; no superposition access to the secret-key encryption device.
assumptions: Approximately floor((pi/4) * 2^128) Grover iterations under the unique-solution assumption.
The plaintext/ciphertext observations are classical. Reversible evaluation under a trial key is a local computation, not a coherent secret-key oracle.
The estimates use logical circuit counts. No conversion to seconds, physical qubits or a demonstrated AES attack is made.
The four-T measurement/feed-forward Toffoli alternative mentioned in the introduction is not the implemented unitary circuit tabulated here.

quantum_model.gate_set: Clifford+T logical gates, with the unitary seven-T Toffoli decomposition used for AES circuits; controlled phase/comparison gates use the source's separate decompositions.
quantum_model.routing: Arbitrary interactions between logical qubits; no nearest-neighbor placement or routing overhead is costed.
quantum_model.error_correction: No physical error-correction, magic-state-factory or hardware runtime cost is included.
quantum_model.oracle_parallelism: 5 parallel AES boxes per candidate-key predicate; compute and uncompute each box. Grover iterations remain sequential.
quantum_model.solution_assumption: Exactly one marked key is assumed after using 5 suitable distinct pairs. Section 3.1 motivates uniqueness heuristically; it is not a proof for actual AES.

time.note: No physical running time is specified. Logical gate counts and circuit depths are separate resource coordinates, not classical AES-operation equivalents.

data.note: Section 3.1 supplies this pair count for a heuristically unique key. Suitable distinct pairs are assumed; this is not a secret-key quantum query count.

memory.note: Classical control/storage memory is not separately priced. Logical qubits are recorded as their own coordinate, not as bytes.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing cost is tabulated for the complete attack.

t_gates.note: Table 5 reports 1.41 × 2^151 T gates. On p.32 the phase operation uses 2024 Toffoli gates or 8108 T gates, but p.41 uses 2024 as a T-gate addend. The same accounting mismatch occurs in arXiv v1. These are not interchangeable units; no corrected total is substituted.

clifford_gates.note: Table 5 complete-search estimate; Section 3.4 explicitly omits some Clifford overhead from controlled operations.

t_depth.note: Table 5 complete-search depth; parallel AES boxes are counted by depth rather than summed as serial calls. The source neglects some non-dominant overhead.

circuit_depth.note: Table 5 complete-search overall depth, not one AES evaluation or wall-clock time. Some non-dominant overhead is neglected.

logical_qubits.note: Table 5 simultaneous logical-qubit estimate (5 AES boxes plus one ancilla). This is not a physical-qubit count.

success.description: Section 2 states high/constant success under the unique-marked-key assumption, without a numerical whole-attack probability; no success value is inferred from the pair-count heuristic.

evidence.interpretation: Complete-search resources are kept separate from reversible AES component costs. Gate/depth coefficients, classical observations, unique-solution assumptions and circuit-level exclusions are retained.

limitations: A logical quantum resource estimate, not a classical black-box cryptanalytic shortcut or a physically executed break.
Gate totals contain a source accounting conflict; T-gate scalar normalization is intentionally absent.
No physical error correction, routing, state distillation, hardware runtime or exact numerical attack success is supplied.

Full result inventory covers component circuits, S-box alternatives and mentioned search schedules. Component circuits and complete-search logical resource estimates are outside active implementation scope; unimplemented inherited search alternatives are not new AES attack configurations. No circuit or attack code was executed.
